product.minus: Every setting is on "download on Wi-Fi only" and background data is off, yet the app burns hundreds of megabytes or gigabytes of cellular data on a short walk. carrier bills and throttling follow

product.title: Background playback versus battery
product.minus: The podcast stops the moment the screen turns off or the app goes to the background. granting background permission fixes that but drains battery several times faster than active screen-on use

product.title: Queue and playlist do whatever they want
product.minus: Drag an episode to a new spot and it snaps back. deleted podcasts reappear. the playlist ignores the chosen order or loops a single episode. "Up Next" plays something the user never picked

product.title: Android Auto and steering-wheel controls break after updates
product.minus: Skip and seek stop working in the car, episode release dates disappear, "safety pause" resets the list. and the car is exactly where people listen most

product.title: Auto-subscribed to shows you never chose
product.minus: The app quietly adds podcasts to your feed that you never subscribed to and starts downloading them. support's advice. "just unsubscribe". lands as a privacy violation

product.title: Endless "rate us" and "upgrade" spam
product.minus: The rating prompt and upgrade banner pop up on every launch, sometimes ten times an hour, even after a review has been submitted and even for paying subscribers. it's the number-one reason users leave one-star reviews

product.title: Tracking consent with no "reject all" button
product.minus: On first launch the app requires manually disabling ad consents one by one from a list of dozens or hundreds of "partners". no single "reject all". privacy-minded users delete it on the spot

product.title: New episodes don't arrive, feed freezes
product.minus: New releases don't appear without a manual refresh or don't come at all, while other apps already have them. subscriptions and history vanish entirely after an update

product.title: Cross-device progress sync breaks
product.plus: When it works, seamless handoff between phone, computer, and tablet is the top reason to stay (Pocket Casts, Player FM web)
product.minus: Listening progress stops syncing: the second device starts from zero, "played" marks reset, everything disappears after a phone swap

product.title: Deep customization and true independence keep users loyal
product.plus: Per-episode speed, intro/outro trimming, playlists, sleep timer, no mandatory account, open-source or one-time payment. users forgive a lot for these and pay voluntarily
product.minus: The wealth of settings turns into a cluttered interface: newcomers struggle to find basic controls and the learning curve drives casual listeners away

product.title: Too many ads, too loud, and layered over speech
product.minus: Dynamic ads are injected over speech and music, play louder than the podcast, and repeat back to back. a 22-minute episode can carry four or five unskippable insertions. the ads outlast the content

product.title: Search can't find a show even by its exact name
product.minus: Type the exact show title and get zero results or irrelevant noise. the same podcast turns up in seconds on Google and Spotify but not in the built-in search

product.title: Developer responds to honest reviews with hostility
product.minus: Replies to anything under five stars are aggressive, blame the user, or paste a template instead of addressing the bug. the responses themselves become a reason to lower the rating and leave

product.title: AI features and "AI-optimized" ads push users to FOSS
product.minus: Surprise generative-AI features and "we now use AI" emails feel like unwanted slop. "AI optimization" in practice means the app's own targeted insertions. enough to send users straight to open-source alternatives

product.title: Silent recording eats the audio. silence instead of an interview
product.minus: The app's core job. reliably capturing audio. fails without a sound: the user believes they're recording, then discovers an empty file or 45 minutes of silence, with no chance to redo it.

product.title: The recording archive vanishes overnight for no reason
product.minus: People build up years of songs, ideas, and legal evidence. then after an update, or simply one morning, everything is gone. This destroys trust in the product as a memory store more thoroughly than any other bug.

product.title: Paywall after recording is the most infuriating pattern in the niche
product.minus: The user records an entire meeting or lecture, waits through the upload, and then sees only 3–5 minutes of transcript behind a paywall. Their content is held hostage at the exact moment when redoing it is impossible.

product.title: Accuracy falls short: dropped words, confused speakers, manual cleanup required
product.minus: The core job. an accurate transcript. is done poorly: whole phrases go missing, errors stack up every sentence, and the user spends more time correcting than they saved. That was the entire reason for getting the app.

product.title: Speaker separation breaks. the real unsolved job for meeting transcription
product.minus: Diarization is the key to transcribing meetings and interviews, yet apps merge two people into one, invent five speakers from a single voice, and give no way to correct the count. Without this, a meeting transcript is useless.

product.title: One language per file. bilingual meetings fall apart
product.minus: Real meetings and lectures often mix two languages, yet the engine handles only one at a time: English terms inside Chinese speech turn into garbage, and accents or non-English speakers are recognized poorly. A huge segment left unserved.

product.title: Transcript comes out in the wrong language. gibberish instead of text
product.minus: An English meeting comes back in Welsh, Afrikaans gets transcribed as German, the language setting is silently ignored. The user receives coherent text in a foreign language and realizes it far too late.

product.title: Transcripts can't leave. text is locked inside the app
product.minus: The "copy summary" button was removed, bulk export doesn't exist, you can only download one recording at a time out of hundreds, and sharing means a link only. Users feel trapped in someone else's software holding their own data.

product.title: Long recordings cut off at 3–5 minutes without warning
product.minus: The recorder quietly stops after a few minutes, clips the beginning, or finalizes the recording the moment you switch away from the app. For lectures and long meetings this makes the product useless exactly where it matters most.

product.title: Call recording requires dialing a service line and merging. it exposes you and it's maddening
product.plus: When it works, it captures both sides cleanly. something free apps can't do.
product.minus: To start recording you have to call a service line and merge the calls. the other person sees "conference call," hears tones, and has already hung up or grown suspicious by the time recording begins. The mechanic gives away that you're taping them.

product.title: Hardware purchase plus subscription on top plus a minute cap = outrage
product.plus: Those who are used to it praise it as a "pocket assistant": transcript and summary ready by the time they're back at their desk.
product.minus: After buying the expensive device, users discover that AI features and any reasonable minute allowance require a separate subscription, and 300 free minutes amounts to fewer than 5 lectures. It feels like paying twice for something a phone does on its own.

product.title: "Why does a voice recorder need my work email and full calendar?". trust collapses at onboarding
product.minus: To record a simple note the app demands sign-in with a work email, calendar access, and contacts. then proceeds to gate-crash others' calls and spam contacts. For a voice recorder, this reads as surveillance.

product.title: Free Gemini, ChatGPT, and Google Recorder are named as direct replacements
product.minus: Users openly write that they upload audio to Gemini or ChatGPT and capture with the free Google Recorder. getting the same or better results for nothing. A paid transcription engine stops being a value proposition on its own.

product.title: "Free trial" = card upfront and charges after cancellation
product.minus: They ask for card details before you've used the app, charge the annual fee immediately after the "trial," keep billing after cancellation, and the subscription doesn't appear in Google Play so you can't stop it. A dedicated churn and chargeback pipeline.

product.title: Transcription only online. dead without internet, and nobody mentions that
product.minus: The advertised offline transcription doesn't work without a connection at all, and constant dependence on signal interrupts dictation mid-sentence. For recording on the road, in a lecture hall, or in a basement this is critical. and undermines trust in every other promise.

product.title: Dictation breaks the flow: pause every 5 seconds, no punctuation, profanity censored
product.minus: For continuous thought-dictation the engine stops every few seconds, adds no punctuation, and even bleeps profanity in private notes. This breaks the entire "I talk, it writes" scenario the product promises.

product.title: AI assistant over recordings searches poorly and digs into all notes
product.plus: The idea of "ask AI across all meetings" resonates. users explicitly request search and queries over their recording library.
product.minus: The promised "ask across all files" in practice does keyword matching, pulls in unrelated notes, and scans private recordings every single time with no way to limit scope. The flagship feature doesn't deliver on its promise.

product.title: Forced 5-star review and pornographic ads at launch. instant uninstall
product.minus: The app locks features until you give five stars, and runs porn-adjacent ads on the start screen. People delete it without trying, warn others about children, and it sends a powerful negative signal across the entire budget-transcriber category.

product.title: Trust as a product: court, job, illness, divorce. the cost of failure is enormous
product.plus: When it works, the product changes lives: it remembers for a long-COVID patient, keeps divorce records, relieves anxiety. The emotional attachment is the strongest in the niche.
product.minus: Those same people use the recorder in critical moments. and failure is not an option. Losing an interview, silence where a lawyer meeting should be, a vanished archive hit the users who need the product most. Reliability here isn't a feature. it is the product.

product.title: Entry disappears mid-typing
product.minus: Sync and auto-save wipe text the user just wrote. people lose hours of writing in an instant

product.title: Your archive held hostage by subscription
product.minus: Subscription lapses and years of entries are locked. no reading, no exporting without paying up first

product.title: New phone wipes years of diary
product.minus: Switching devices silently deletes old entries. users only find out about backups after everything is gone

product.title: The "lifetime" license they took back
product.minus: Paid once and owned it forever. then years later forced to pay again, and old purchase receipts "don't count"

product.title: No support. just a bot going in circles
product.minus: Reports of lost data and billing issues go unanswered for weeks. the only channel is an AI chat that leads nowhere

product.title: Bold text and a second journal cost extra
product.minus: Basics. italics, headings, a second notebook, dark mode. are all paywalled

product.title: The paid lock doesn't lock
product.minus: A journal about the most personal things stays wide open: PIN fails, screen stays visible, desktop has no lock at all

product.title: Forgotten password = archive sealed forever
product.minus: Lose your PIN or encryption key and there's no reset. years of entries are permanently entombed

product.title: A paywall and mandatory tasks before the first entry
product.minus: No chance to try it first: payment screen, a compulsory "5-day challenge," required account, and consent flows all upfront

product.title: Free-trial trap
product.minus: "3 days free" charges the card immediately, cancellation is buried on the website, and refunds don't happen

product.title: AI in a diary feels like an intrusion, not help
product.minus: Forced AI features read the most personal content. there's no off switch. users leave on principle

product.title: "On this day" a year ago. the hook that keeps people coming back
product.plus: Reminders about entries from past years spark reflection and bring users back to the app every single day

product.title: Prompts beat the blank page
product.plus: Questions and templates get people who "never journaled" writing. there's always something to start from each day

product.title: One-time purchase. a flag against subscriptions
product.plus: "Bought it once and it's mine forever". the top reason people love these apps and switch from competitors

product.title: A photo on every entry. the ritual that keeps users
product.plus: Attaching a photo to each entry turns the journal into a memory collage and becomes a beloved daily habit

product.title: Cross-device sync. but only if you pay
product.minus: Writing on phone and reading on laptop. the core use case. either breaks or sits behind a paywall

product.title: Cursor jumps, words duplicate
product.minus: The editor jumps to the top on its own and repeats words mid-edit. writing anything long becomes impossible

product.title: Voice and handwriting. demand that nobody has met
product.minus: Users want to dictate or write with a stylus, especially when ill or when their hands are tired. the feature simply doesn't exist

product.title: AI-generated interpretations kill trust in the reading
product.minus: Introducing "AI readings" feels like a desecration of the practice: users stop believing anything real stands behind a spread and delete the app in a rush of emotion

product.title: A card from a random-number generator is not a drawn card
product.minus: Experienced practitioners feel the difference between pseudo-random and genuine card selection. when a spread is computer-generated, the whole point of tarot disappears and the app is written off as a fake

product.title: Lifetime access was silently converted into a subscription
product.minus: A "Pro forever" purchase made years ago was voided, ads were brought back, and a subscription was demanded. this reads as fraud and destroys trust in the developer permanently

product.title: Blaring ads mid-reading break the meditative state
product.minus: Full-screen video ads with a separate volume control blast at maximum while users are concentrating. this directly contradicts what a reflection-and-stillness app is supposed to be

product.title: An ad for every single card pull. spiritual app as a cash register
product.minus: The daily card used to be free. now a single pull requires watching a video or paying a dollar a day. it reads as greed that is fundamentally incompatible with a spiritual niche

product.title: Earned points wiped out and unlocked content locked away again
product.minus: Users spent years accumulating points and unlocking cards, then an update reset everything and hid it behind a paywall. the feeling of having something earned taken away is the single biggest trigger for deletion and anger

product.title: Best companion for learning. understanding card meanings and symbolism
product.plus: The core reason for five-star reviews: people come to learn to read tarot, and an app that explains meanings, symbols, and their interplay becomes "the one"

product.title: Digital companion to a physical deck. look up meanings without the book
product.plus: A large segment owns a real deck and wants the app as a reference: draw with your hands, look up the meaning, save the spread. a distinct job, not a fortune-teller

product.title: Card of the day and a widget. the backbone of a daily ritual
product.plus: A card-of-the-day widget starts a habit: people open the app every morning and weave the reading into their routine. a broken widget shatters exactly the habit that keeps them around
product.minus: The widget stops updating or tapping, the daily card arrives at a random time. a technical failure kills the very habit the app was kept for

product.title: Spread journal and years of entries lost during migration
product.plus: A log of saved spreads is what people come back to for years and use to trace their path
product.minus: Shutting down the old app and migrating wiped years of entries without warning or any export option. losing a personal history hurts more than losing money

product.title: Control over reversed cards and spread distribution
product.minus: The algorithm gives either too many reversals or only positive cards. nothing like a real deck. users explicitly ask for a reversal-probability slider

product.title: Symbolic depth was stripped away to chase mass appeal
product.minus: The updated version removed detailed interpretations, chakra links, numerology, I Ching, and literary references. leaving generic "something for everyone" copy that drained the app of all value

product.title: Asking for phone number, location, and an account feels intrusive in an intimate practice
product.minus: A simple card pull now demands a phone number, birthday, location, and mandatory sign-up. in what is essentially a private practice, this reads as data harvesting and drives users away

product.title: A coin or gem economy layered on top of a subscription feels like a scam
product.minus: After paying for a subscription you still have to buy coins for each reading. updates silently wipe coin balances. the double-charge setup feels like deception

product.title: Resonance and uncanny accuracy. the reason people love this niche
product.plus: The core value of the entire niche: when a spread lands on exactly what is happening right now, it produces an almost mystical sense of wonder that creates loyalty lasting years. accuracy is what keeps users

product.title: "Just let me shuffle and draw". against feature bloat
product.minus: Part of the audience wants the minimum: shuffle, draw, read the meaning. layers of sections, categories, and social features read as cognitive load and a reason to uninstall

product.title: "First chat free". the bait behind paid consultations
product.minus: The promised free first consultation never materialises. readers stall on replies to rack up per-minute charges. the live-reader chat model is widely perceived as a con

product.title: Reminders quietly die after a couple of days
product.minus: The core feature. a nudge to drink water. stops working within 1–3 days in most apps and only fires while the user actively has the app open

product.title: The day ends at midnight. and night owls lose their progress
product.minus: Night owls and shift workers can't shift the day boundary: the counter resets at 00:00, water logged after midnight doesn't count, and motivation tanks

product.title: A cute companion turns hydration into a habit
product.plus: A living thing. a plant, a fish, a llama, a water drop. that thrives on what you drink turns a dull routine into caring for something. it's the single biggest driver of long-term retention

product.title: Gamification breaks. and takes the motivation with it
product.minus: Streaks and rewards are the engine of habit, but they collapse from a missed day, a bug, or a phone switch. a broken day-counter isn't just a glitch, it removes the entire point of the app

product.title: Smart reminders vs. a dumb timer
product.plus: Reminders that factor in how much you've already drunk and when, adapting throughout the day, are valued above everything else. it's a coach, not an alarm

product.title: Coffee and water count the same. and that's wrong
product.minus: Users want coffee, tea, and alcohol counted by hydration coefficient (or subtracted), not treated as pure water. otherwise the number is already lying by mid-morning

product.title: A watch tile and widget with one tap. that's what keeps people
product.plus: A watch complication and a "poured. tapped" widget eliminate the friction of logging. these are the features people actually pay for and stick around for years because of

product.title: A widget that just opens the app is useless
product.minus: A widget should add a glass straight from the home screen. if it merely launches the app. and shows an ad before you can log anything. the whole point of quick logging is lost

product.title: Can't edit or delete a past log entry
product.minus: People back-fill entries or get the amount wrong. with no way to undo or edit a record, users feel like they're lying to their own tracker. and switch to a competitor

product.title: Switched phones. lost everything: data, streak, purchase
product.minus: No reliable sync or backup: changing phones wipes out years of progress and voids a paid subscription, and restore purchases doesn't bring it back

product.title: Health integration is advertised but doesn't work
product.minus: Health Connect, Fitbit, Google Fit, Samsung Health. the main reason people install and pay. but the sync keeps breaking or gets blocked by Google

product.title: Team and family mode as a habit driver
product.plus: Competing with friends and family accountability sustain motivation. but cross-platform support (iOS↔Android) is almost always broken

product.title: Ads block the very act of logging water
product.minus: Not ordinary ads. a strategic failure: a full-screen video every time you tap "add water" makes the primary action impossible and drives users straight to a competitor

product.title: Basic features behind a paywall kill trust on first launch
product.minus: Locking a custom goal, dark mode, non-water drinks, and history history behind a paywall reads as greed and destroys trust before the user has even tried the app

product.title: Bought it "forever". now it's gone
product.minus: Lifetime and one-time purchases disappear after an update, a sign-in, or a device switch, and "restore purchases" doesn't bring them back. a fatal blow to paying users' trust

product.title: Medical need and neurodivergence. not "fitness". are the real use case
product.plus: The strongest reason to install: kidney stones, bariatric surgery, diuretic medications, ADHD, elderly users with a diminished sense of thirst. this is a clinical scenario, not a cosmetic one

product.title: "Drink less". the forgotten fluid-restriction scenario
product.minus: Some users need to limit fluid intake on medical advice, not increase it. every app only pushes upward and distorts figures with coefficients. a gap no one has filled

product.title: A quiet, low-pressure tone beats an aggressive one
product.plus: A gentle, guilt-free nudge and a soft "water" sound are what users love. an alarm-style notification that overrides system volume settings drives uninstalls

product.title: Too many features kill simplicity
product.minus: A portion of the audience just wants "remind me and count". an interface stuffed with icons, mini-games, and upsells gets described as overstimulating and sends users to minimalist alternatives

product.title: Deleted emails keep rising from the dead
product.minus: The single most widespread pain in the category: a user deletes, archives, or sorts emails into folders, and after the next sync they surface right back in the inbox. sometimes instantly, sometimes an hour later. People end up deleting the same email three to six times before giving up and switching to an app where deletion actually sticks.

product.title: Notifications go silent. you only know mail arrived by opening the app
product.minus: Push notifications randomly stop working, arrive hours late, or never come at all. The most basic promise of an email client. "tell me when something arrives". breaks down, and users miss things that matter. For apps that run without Google services (Tuta, Proton) this is a structural weakness.

product.title: Emails take a minute to open. the client is slower than the web
product.minus: Opening a message, refreshing the list, hitting send. every action takes seconds or even minutes. Users drift back to the web interface or to Gmail itself because the third-party client is slower than the underlying service it sits on top of.

product.title: Blocking a sender costs money
product.minus: The most common complaint about paywalls: blocking a sender. something Gmail does for free. is locked behind a subscription. People reach for "Block" in a moment of frustration, hit a paywall, and immediately go block that sender in Gmail instead.

product.title: Forced AI: the button won't go away and it hijacks replies
product.minus: A permanent AI button stuck in the toolbar, an assistant that pops up every time you reply, and in some cases an app that sends messages with its own signature without asking. A large and vocal group of users explicitly writes "we don't want AI, give us a working email app". and leaves over a feature they never asked for.

product.title: An update broke the app they loved
product.minus: A recurring pattern across the category: "used it for years. the latest update killed it." A new UI hides familiar features, resets settings, breaks search and sync. Bluemail and Yahoo take the hardest hit: loyal users of five to ten years leave waves of 1-star reviews after redesigns.

product.title: "Free" turns out to be a paywall at the door
product.minus: Spike dropped its free tier and now pushes a subscription the moment you open the app. Aqua Mail and Tuta advertise "free" but let you add only one account or ask for a card upfront. Users feel bait-and-switched and write "scam". while the store rating still reflects the old free version.

product.title: Unified inbox. the whole reason people install the app
product.plus: The one value that earns consistent praise: all mailboxes in one place, no account-switching. Edison, Bluemail, and Canary retain users on exactly this. "one screen for Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, and iCloud." Outlook still hasn't shipped a proper unified inbox.

product.title: Emails don't send or arrive without supervision
product.minus: Messages get stuck in Outbox, "Sent" turns out to be a lie, and sending only works while the app is open. For anyone using email professionally, this destroys trust: you can't rely on a message actually having left your hands.

product.title: The spam filter doesn't learn. you block it, it comes back
product.minus: Marking something as spam doesn't stick: the same sender lands in the inbox again and again, sometimes dozens of times. Aqua loses users to eM Client specifically over this. Bluemail stopped filtering altogether after an update. A filter that actually remembers is a real, unaddressed need.

product.title: Privacy. the one thing people endure everything else for
product.plus: Proton's and Tuta's clean, surveillance-free approach creates genuine fans: no ads, no tracking, "de-Googling." It's the only axis on which users forgive weak search and slow sync. A strong brand narrative that competitors can't easily copy.

product.title: Search is either broken or locked behind a paywall
product.minus: Proton has been missing in-app search for years. Tuta's indexing takes hours and doesn't survive a restart. Bluemail and Yahoo broke search in an update. Finding last year's receipt for a warranty claim is genuinely painful. A core feature, still unresolved.

product.title: Sign-up wall: banned before you send your first email
product.minus: A pain unique to privacy-first services: when creating an account, your IP gets flagged for "abuse prevention," the captcha loops endlessly, manual approval takes 24–48 hours. and that approval requires you to send an email from the account that isn't approved yet. People leave for Proton before they've read a single message.

product.title: Accounts keep dropping. constant re-authentication
product.minus: Outlook, Hotmail, and Google accounts regularly "lose credentials," forcing users to re-enter passwords across three mailboxes. often after an update or just every couple of days at random. It kills the fundamental expectation of "log in once and it works."

product.title: Outlook and Microsoft accounts connect worse than anything else
product.minus: A gap that runs through every third-party client: Google accounts add smoothly, while Outlook, Office 365, and Hotmail hang, require admin approval, or simply reject credentials. This is particularly damaging because "better than Outlook" is the main reason people switch in the first place.

product.title: All-or-nothing pricing. no room for one honest inbox
product.minus: A pricing gap: a user wants one or two small things (auto-empty trash, remove signature, one extra address), but the only option is an expensive bundle with VPN, storage, and AI they don't want. A direct, repeated ask for a cheap micro-tier. "99 cents for what I actually need". goes unheard.

product.title: Full-screen ads before you can read a message
product.minus: Mainly an Aqua Mail and Yahoo problem: unskippable video ads that sometimes run pornographic or Temu banners, playing for up to two minutes between every action. A professional user can't read a work email without waiting out an ad. app deleted immediately.

product.title: Gamified email nobody asked for. streaks in a mail app
product.minus: Yahoo layered daily streaks, achievements, and audio cues on top of an email inbox. The reaction is unanimous: "this is email, not a game, just let me read my messages." A clear signal that manufacturing engagement with artificial metrics drives people away.

product.title: Account recovery equals losing your emails forever
product.minus: The dark side of end-to-end encryption: forget or reset your password and old emails are encrypted and gone for good. Recovery methods (old device, key file) are not built for ordinary people. The real fear of losing years of email keeps many people from switching to a private service.

product.title: Tablets and foldables: the interface just stretches
product.minus: No dual-pane mode on tablets, foldables, or Chromebooks. the phone UI simply scales up, readability suffers, and deleting a message snaps the view to the accounts list. iOS clients usually handle this. Android ones don't. A whole niche. email for large screens. sits unclaimed.

product.title: GPS rangefinder replacing the laser. the core job people install the app for
product.plus: When distances are accurate to within a couple of yards, players ditch the laser rangefinder from their bag and trust the phone on every shot
product.minus: Any slip in accuracy wipes out that trust instantly: one wrong number and the user switches to a competitor

product.title: Android watches don't work. and that's exactly why people bought the app
product.plus: When the watch actually runs, players get through a round without pulling out their phone, and that's what they consider the real value
product.minus: On Galaxy and Pixel watches the app loses GPS, freezes, or crashes on launch. forcing players to reach for their phone on every shot anyway

product.title: The watch goes to sleep between shots. players have to reopen the app dozens of times per round
product.minus: The watch screen turns off and the app drops to the background. to see the distance you have to relaunch it. while wearing a glove and walking, that kills the pace of play

product.title: Android is a second-class citizen: features ship on iPhone while Android users wait indefinitely
product.minus: For the same $200 a year, Android users get a cut-down experience. no green maps, no auto-tracking, no new features. and the developers won't even give a release date

product.title: Auto shot-tracking catches phantom swings and misses real ones. players spend the round babysitting the app
product.plus: When tracking hits 90-plus percent accuracy, club and distance data genuinely changes club selection and lowers handicap
product.minus: Sensors and smart mode either add a shot every time the player stops, or drop half the real shots. so the player watches the app instead of playing golf

product.title: Post-round editing is the hidden tax on tracking
product.minus: After every round you have to manually add missed shots, fix clubs and holes. on top of that the editor crashes. 10 to 20 minutes of cleanup instead of enjoying the game

product.title: Holes don't advance on their own and jump around. scores end up on the wrong hole
product.minus: The app either makes you manually swipe to the next hole or advances on its own at the wrong moment. players record scores in the wrong place and lose faith in the scorecard

product.title: Course maps are outdated, broken, or missing. and developers blame Google Maps
product.minus: The home course is absent or was captured in winter under snow during renovation. support says it depends on Google updates and the wait can stretch to years

product.title: Live group scoring and a friends feed. the reason golf stays a social game
product.plus: Seeing in real time how playing partners and friends on other courses are doing turns a solo round into a shared experience and keeps a group inside one app
product.minus: Leaderboards and group scoring break, get hidden behind a paywall, or require everyone to download the app. and the social value collapses

product.title: Stats and strokes gained. the "make me better" job people are willing to pay for
product.plus: Players see where they're losing shots, make more deliberate swings, and drop several handicap strokes over a season. that's the justification for the price
product.minus: When an update breaks the stats section or hides strokes gained behind a paywall, the core value disappears and the user leaves

product.title: AI caddie and club suggestion. a promise that more often annoys than helps
product.plus: When the caddie accounts for wind, elevation, and the player's real distances, the advice to "take one more club" puts the ball on the green and earns genuine delight
product.minus: Recommendations are often absurd. the same club for 100 and 140 yards, or a driver plus two wedges on a par 4. and trust in the AI collapses

product.title: Screen unreadable in bright sunlight. a basic failure for an outdoor app
product.minus: Dark, small text and a screen dimmed to save battery can't be read in sunlight. on a low-resolution aerial image hazards like water are invisible

product.title: Phone in the pocket advances holes and logs shots on its own. phone-based tracking is unreliable
product.minus: Without a separate sensor, the phone in a pocket registers accidental touches that change settings, add clubs, and even end the round. a screen lock is essential

product.title: Offline mode fails where there's no signal. and courses often have no coverage
product.minus: Maps don't load without internet even when the course was preloaded. on remote courses with no signal the app is useless and drains the battery searching for a network

product.title: Handicap (GHIN / WHS) won't link. yet that's half the reason people install the app
product.plus: Direct score posting to GHIN / USGA is the reason players tolerate every other flaw and don't leave
product.minus: Outside the US the World Handicap System isn't supported. inside the US, handicap now requires a separate paid GHIN subscription on top of the app

product.title: Subscription bait-and-switch: things paid for "forever" cost money again, and cancellation is hidden
product.minus: Lifetime or one-time purchases get wiped on an update and replaced with an annual subscription. prices jump several times over. free trials charge immediately with no visible cancel button

product.title: Swing video analysis matters most with a coach, but the tools are locked behind a subscription
product.plus: Recording, slow motion, drawing lines, and comparing with tour players genuinely help beginners and connect student and instructor in one place
product.minus: Basic tools. lines, video import. are now paywalled. on Android recording is capped at 30 fps and the app crashes. without a subscription it's just a camera

product.title: Ads and upgrade pop-ups appear on every shot. even for paying subscribers
product.minus: Video ads and premium upsell prompts appear at round start and between holes, breaking the pace of play. and they show up even for users who already have a paid subscription

product.title: An annual subscription makes no sense where the season is only six months
product.minus: In northern regions courses are under snow for half the year, yet pricing is annual-only. players cancel en masse and ask for a monthly option

product.title: Battery dies during a round. phone or watch doesn't survive to the 18th hole
product.minus: GPS mode and background tracking drain a fully charged phone by the 13th or 14th hole, and watches don't make it to the end of the round. the app stops being reliable

product.title: Editing past fasting times
product.minus: Users regularly forget to tap Start or Stop, and the fast is gone for good. Most apps have no editing of past entries at all, or the edit breaks the log with a "cannot overlap fasts" error on any attempt.

product.title: Lock screen widget and live timer
product.plus: When the widget works, users love it: no need to open the app, fast progress is visible at a glance. Some apps support Dynamic Island and the lock screen, and those get called out specifically.
product.minus: Widgets are the most fragile part: after an update they stop refreshing, show the wrong window, or lose connection to Apple Watch. Users leave specifically because of this bug.

product.title: History and data loss after an update or new device
product.minus: Reinstalling or updating the app wipes months of fasting history and weight data. Most apps have no real cloud backup, and users find out only after the data is already gone.

product.title: Fasting phases and educational content in the timer
product.plus: Showing the current biological phase directly on the timer (fat burning, ketosis, autophagy) is the top motivational trigger. Users hold out longer when they can see what is happening in their body right now.
product.minus: Phase content is often shallow or cuts off mid-way: it shows only the first 24 hours, does not explain autophagy, and is not adapted to the user's protocol (16:8 vs OMAD).

product.title: Sync across iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch
product.minus: There is no shared state across devices: a fast started on the phone is invisible on the watch and vice versa. Users are forced to duplicate actions manually, and that is exactly why they leave.

product.title: Start and end reminders
product.plus: Reminders are the second most important retention mechanic: users want a notification 30 minutes before the eating window closes and an alert when the fast is set to begin. The ones who get this working do not leave.
product.minus: Reminders fire inconsistently or not at all. Several apps have no audible alert, only a silent notification the user misses. Some users get notifications at random times unrelated to their fast.

product.title: Protocol schedules and presets (16:8, 18:6, OMAD)
product.plus: Ready-made presets (16:8, 18:6) reduce start friction. Users value being able to pick a protocol and skip doing the window math themselves.
product.minus: Flexibility is limited: non-standard rhythms (19:5, 21:3) are not available, and alternate-day fasting with an irregular schedule is not supported. BodyFast forces users to rebuild the schedule from scratch every week with no option to save the previous one.

product.title: Streak counter and consecutive-day tracking
product.plus: A visual streak is the key retention hook: users hold on for the number and feel the loss when it breaks. Apps where the streak is clear and fair earn loyal audiences.
product.minus: The streak algorithm often does not count fasts longer than a day (Fasta treats 25+ hours as a missed day) or resets due to technical glitches. One reset wipes months of effort and people quit the app.

product.title: Weight and body metrics tracking
product.plus: A visual weight-loss curve is a powerful motivator. Users want to see the chart inside the app, next to fasting history, without switching to Apple Health.
product.minus: The weight chart is either missing, breaks after updates, or syncs with Apple Health only one way: data goes out but never comes back. Historical weight data disappears after updates, right when the user has something to show for it.

product.title: Heavy onboarding and friction before the first fast
product.plus: Apps that let you tap Start immediately without 15 questions earn five stars specifically for that. Time to first fast is the single biggest factor in first impressions.
product.minus: Most apps load users with long questionnaires (20-30 questions) followed immediately by a paywall. People feel deceived and delete the app before they ever start a fast.

product.title: Goal pressure and aggressive food criticism
product.minus: Apps that comment on every meal and flag "wrong" foods irritate even loyal users. Automated tips are read as judgment, not support, and the person stops logging food.

product.title: Eating window timer alongside the fasting timer
product.plus: Users increasingly want to see not just a fasting countdown but how much time is left in their eating window. This shifts the frame from "how long have I been fasting" to "do I still have time to eat."
product.minus: Most apps show only one timer: the fast. An eating window countdown is almost nowhere to be found, even though users request it across multiple different apps.

product.title: Route sends you onto dangerous roads
product.minus: Route planners direct cyclists onto highways, high-speed roads, and unshouldered carriageways while ignoring the bike path running right alongside

product.title: Route leads into roads that don't exist
product.minus: Cyclists get sent through rivers, minefields, and dead ends on trails that have no real-world counterpart

product.title: Voice cues arrive late or not at all
product.minus: Turn announcements fire half a kilometre too early, lag behind the turn, or never come. forcing riders to stare at the screen while moving

product.title: Left and right confused, no rerouting when off course
product.minus: When a turn is missed the app fails to reroute or recenter the map, instead looping "make a U-turn" indefinitely

product.title: Can't set a custom start point
product.minus: The planner locks onto the current location and gives no way to set a home address or any other start point

product.title: Background recording stops and loses the whole ride
product.minus: Switch away from the app or let the screen go dark and tracking halts. at the finish line there's nothing saved

product.title: GPS draws straight lines and cuts distance in half
product.minus: Tracks jump between points in straight lines, route through buildings, and report half the distance actually ridden

product.title: New Android and Samsung phones kill the tracker
product.minus: After Android 16 updates and on Samsung devices apps lose GPS lock, go dormant, and stay broken even with all battery restrictions lifted

product.title: Sensors and heart rate monitors won't stay connected
product.minus: Bluetooth heart rate, speed, and cadence sensors are either unsupported or get stripped from the screen mid-ride by an update

product.title: Komoot turned intrusive after it was sold
product.minus: Since the Bending Spoons acquisition the app buries users in subscription pop-ups. even those who already paid for lifetime map access

product.title: Paid for maps, then lost access
product.minus: Lifetime map and region purchases stop working, restore-purchase flows return errors, and users are dropped back onto a free trial

product.title: Paid software drains the battery mid-ride
product.minus: Navigation during a ride kills the phone in a couple of hours with no warning and no track-free navigation mode

product.title: Can't see the app before handing over payment details
product.minus: The app demands card details before showing what it can do, so cyclists end up paying blindly for something they haven't tried

product.title: Basic navigation locked behind a paywall
product.minus: Without a subscription there is nothing to do except browse. saving, building, or actually riding a route all require payment

product.title: Subscribing is easy. cancelling is a trap
product.minus: Cancellation is buried outside the app, charges still land after users cancel, and refunds for broken trials are refused

product.title: Expensive hardware demands constant updates and then crashes
product.minus: Paid indoor software downloads gigabytes of updates before every ride, hangs halfway through, and can wipe out an hour-long session

product.title: Smart trainer won't even connect to the brand's own hardware
product.minus: Virtual shifting and smart trainers drop their Bluetooth connection mid-ride. often with the same brand's own equipment

product.title: Real-video routes keep you on the trainer longer
product.plus: Footage of actual roads rather than a cartoon world motivates riders to spin for hours and pulls them away from Zwift

product.title: Watch and bike computer keep disconnecting
product.minus: The phone-to-watch and phone-to-head-unit link drops multiple times a day, and re-syncing requires manual re-pairing every time

product.title: Ending a ride takes eight unnecessary taps
product.minus: Finishing a ride means clicking through six to eight confirmation screens, and the forced save of every outing makes it worse

product.title: Kids crack the block in a day. the arms race is already lost
product.minus: Children bypass protection through Safe Mode, factory resets, Samsung Secure Folder, guest profiles, or simply googling "how to bypass". parents pay for the illusion of control.

product.title: Bonus time expires but the phone stays wide open for hours
product.minus: You grant 30 minutes, the timer runs out, but the device never re-locks. and the kid plays until midnight. Command sync failures gut the entire point of the app.

product.title: Teenagers feel imprisoned. the app destroys family trust
product.minus: Kids write that they cry themselves to sleep, lose friends, and resent their parents. the feeling of being surveilled pushes them to hide rather than open up.

product.title: Ambient listening. a feature kids call straight-up spying
product.minus: The ability to listen to the microphone in real time crosses a line: kids fear being recorded in the bathroom and shower, feeling like a pet rather than a person.

product.title: Bark's AI flags a frog as porn while real threats slip through
product.plus: When it fires correctly it saves the day. catching bullying, peer pressure, and dangerous conversations and opening important family dialogues.
product.minus: False positives (a statue, "that's sick", a pet photo) bury the real signal, while genuinely dangerous texts and videos walk right past.

product.title: Location freezes for hours. parent panic instead of peace of mind
product.minus: GPS still shows the child at school hours after they got home, "no activity for 24 hours," or the child "in the ocean". that's exactly what the app was installed for, and it fails at the moment it matters.

product.title: Geofences spam all night. "left home / arrived home" on repeat
product.minus: Dozens of false arrival-and-departure alerts while the child sleeps devalue every notification and force parents to mute the phone. killing the entire purpose of alerts.

product.title: Over-blocking: the bank app, settings, school sites, split screen
product.minus: Blocks picture-in-picture, split screen, the banking app, the voice assistant, and explicitly allowed school sites. the phone becomes useless for everyday life.

product.title: Uninstall protection turns against the parent. locked out of their own phone
product.minus: Parents cannot remove the app even after cancelling their subscription, the phone bricks without a PIN, and adults get mistakenly flagged as children.

product.title: Cross-platform gap: Android parent can't monitor the kid's iPhone
product.plus: Mobicip and OurPact earn praise specifically for one set of settings that works across every device. phone, tablet, and laptop on iOS and Android alike.
product.minus: Most apps don't let an Android parent manage a teenager's iPhone, and pairing requires a computer and USB cable that many families simply don't have.

product.title: No way to "graduate" a child. control either vanishes at 13 or suffocates until 18
product.minus: Family Link offers almost nothing after 13 and lets teenagers remove supervision themselves. paid apps have no smooth mechanism for handing freedom back as kids grow up.

product.title: Floating-window loophole kills the screen-time limit
product.minus: A child opens a blocked app in picture-in-picture or split screen, or instantly reopens it from recents. and the time limit simply doesn't apply.

product.title: Drains the kid's battery dead by midday
product.minus: Background tracking and the VPN drain the battery many times faster than normal: Bark watches hitting 11% by 4 pm, idle consumption jumping from 1% to 16% per hour. the device stops being a communication tool.

product.title: "Blame the app": the rules come from the software, not the parent
product.plus: The biggest win for loyal parents. the child's anger at YouTube shutting off at 6 pm lands on the app, not on mom and dad. fewer arguments.

product.title: Human support. the one thing Mobicip has that abandoned competitors don't
product.plus: A real person responds within a day and actually solves the problem. against bots and silence at Bark, OurPact, and FamiSafe, this becomes the top reason families stay.

product.title: Bark phone as a product: parent peace of mind, teenager humiliation
product.plus: A ready-made "kids" phone and watch lowers the entry barrier: approve contacts and apps, see the location. a solid first device for younger children.
product.minus: For a teenager it's a "helicopter phone" with little-kid branding: lags, eats storage, friends mock it, and there's no marketing aimed at teens.

product.title: Billing trap: charged after cancellation, unsubscribe only by email
product.minus: No cancel button, annual charge fires after "cancellation," refunds denied. a distinct class of abuse, not ordinary price complaints.

product.title: Text and call monitoring either goes silent or dumps an unreadable mess
product.minus: Test swear words and conversations go uncaught, incoming messages are invisible, and captured messages land in a jumbled pile with no contact grouping. following a conversation is impossible.

product.title: Order marked delivered. no food at the door: refunds routinely denied
product.minus: The courier marks the order "delivered," nothing shows up, and the platform hides behind its own GPS stamp to deny the refund

product.title: Half the order missing. and they hand you a five-dollar credit
product.minus: Half the order doesn't arrive, and the remedy is a token credit. they won't reship the missing items

product.title: Price at the door doubles: fees cost more than the food itself
product.minus: The final checkout total is one and a half to two times the menu price once markups and service fees pile on

product.title: No real support: a bot in an endless loop instead of a human
product.minus: Help means a chatbot cycling through the same canned replies, with no phone number and no path to a live agent

product.title: Courier took two or three orders. food arrives cold
product.minus: The platform stacks multiple orders on one driver, and your meal sits cooling in the bag while he finishes someone else's run

product.title: Promised 20 minutes. you wait two hours
product.minus: The quoted delivery time is bait. once you pay, the estimate quietly shifts an hour or two later

product.title: Can't cancel: you pay in full for an order that never happens
product.minus: Cancellation is blocked even seconds after placing the order, and if the restaurant is closed or no driver is available you still get charged in full plus a cancellation fee

product.title: Promo-code bait: the discount vanishes at checkout
product.minus: A big first-order discount is advertised, but at the payment step the code fails to apply or the system asks you to remove it and charges full price

product.title: Courier steals the food. the platform looks the other way
product.minus: The driver takes or eats the order, and the platform neither penalises them nor refunds you. the thief simply picks up the next job

product.title: Subscription snuck in, impossible to cancel
product.minus: A premium membership is slipped in with one tap at checkout and charged immediately, while cancellation sends you through an endless menu maze

product.title: Tips demanded upfront, before the work is done. with no way to adjust
product.minus: Tips are required before delivery, calculated on the full fee-inflated total, and can't be reduced afterward even if the food arrives cold or an hour late

product.title: Unauthorised substitutions: they send whatever they feel like
product.minus: Pickers and restaurants ignore substitution instructions, send the wrong item or near-expired products, and treat it as perfectly normal

product.title: Spoiled and unsafe food. no replacement, no refund
product.minus: Rotten meat, mouldy bread, and melted ice cream show up at the door, and a food-safety complaint is met with a flat refusal

product.title: Address lost: driver can't find the building
product.minus: The app defaults to a stale or wrong address, the driver doesn't call, and the bag gets dropped at the wrong location instead of the right door

product.title: PIN code at the door: trust burden shifted onto the customer
product.minus: One past complaint gets you forced to read out a code at every future delivery. the driver sits outside and won't hand over the food until you do

product.title: When a real person steps in, the customer stays for years
product.plus: A fast refund, a fixed problem, and a courteous driver who carries groceries inside turns a one-off order into years of loyalty

product.title: A lifeline for people who can't leave home
product.plus: For people without a car, those with disabilities, the elderly, and post-surgery patients, delivery isn't a convenience. it's the only way to eat

product.title: Forced AI instead of a store: loyal users switch to rivals
product.minus: A mandatory AI assistant (Grok/SpaceX) replaced the familiar browse-by-category layout, slows the app down, and can't be dismissed. loyal customers are leaving

product.title: Ratings and reviews hidden: trust in stars destroyed
product.minus: The platform conceals real customer reviews and inflates star ratings, turning restaurant selection into a lottery

product.title: Price creeps up with every repeat order
product.minus: Opening the same dish a second time shows a higher price than before. users suspect surveillance-based dynamic pricing

product.title: The algorithm ignores the song you actually picked
product.minus: You tap a specific track and the service plays "recommended songs you might like" instead. or dumps you straight into forced shuffle. It is the defining humiliation of both free and paid listeners.

product.title: "Downloaded" is a lie: offline tracks won't play without internet
product.minus: People pay specifically for offline access, download a playlist, then see "you are offline" or an endless spinner on the plane or commute. the downloaded files keep reaching for the network anyway.

product.title: Music cuts out mid-track: "network error" after every song
product.minus: Even on strong Wi-Fi a track stalls after a minute or throws a "network issue" banner after every song. the only fix is force-quitting and relaunching the app.

product.title: A redesign broke habits that worked for years
product.minus: The widget, artist page, queue, and lyrics view were rebuilt without asking. and came out worse. Familiar gestures vanished, and there is no way to go back to the old version.

product.title: The catalog is shrinking: favorite albums disappear without warning
product.minus: Songs and entire albums from major artists vanish from the library. licensing changes or ownership shifts. while playlists quietly hollow out over the years with no notification.

product.title: AI-generated music is flooding feeds. listeners want a block button
product.minus: Mixes, stations, and artist pages are filling up with AI-generated tracks uploaded under real artists' names. Users are explicitly asking for an "AI-made" label, a report button, and a way to block it permanently.

product.title: Leaving Spotify on ethical grounds. then disappointed by the replacement
product.plus: A whole wave of users is migrating from Spotify over fair artist pay and distaste for certain ad campaigns. Deezer and Tidal are catching this demand as a ready-made segment.
product.minus: But the new home greets them with bugs, broken search, and a clunky interface, and some migrants regret switching.

product.title: Casting, Android Auto, and speaker connections keep dropping
product.minus: In the car and on speakers the service endlessly reconnects, loses the link, or simply stops appearing as an available app. yet those are precisely the places people listen most.

product.title: Stations and recommendations mash genres into a muddy blend
product.minus: Radio and algorithms inject completely unrelated genres. rap bleeding into a country station, Sam Smith surfacing on a classic-guitar channel. and there is no way to build a clean single-genre stream.

product.title: Shuffle cycles through the same handful of songs instead of the whole playlist
product.minus: A playlist has hundreds of tracks, yet the service loops through the same forty. even on paid tiers. The "random" order is predictable, and there is no way to exclude a shared playlist from affecting your taste profile.

product.title: The service swaps out the exact version of a track you saved
product.minus: A liked remix, bass-boost edit, or studio recording gets silently replaced with the original or an acoustic version after an update. the specific version the listener loved is just gone.

product.title: Identically named artists get merged into one page, and reporting does nothing
product.minus: Musicians who share a name get lumped onto a single page, mixing each other's albums into release notifications, with no way for users to fix the metadata themselves.

product.title: It forgets where you left off: every session starts from scratch
product.minus: Open the app in the morning and it resumes a track from a search you ran a week ago instead of the playlist you left yesterday. In the car there is no auto-resume and no way to continue from the same spot.

product.title: The queue and "play next" simply do not work
product.minus: You add tracks to the queue and they never actually play in order, or they land at the very end behind auto-generated content. One accidental tap on a song further down wipes the whole hand-built queue.

product.title: Search can't find even an exact track title
product.minus: Type the full song name and artist and get "nothing found". or a wall of irrelevant covers. Search breaks whenever the catalog hasn't finished loading, and there are no useful filters.

product.title: Canceling a subscription is impossible. charges continue after cancellation
product.minus: There is no cancel button, or it leads only to a payment-method change screen. Users keep getting billed for months after canceling, with no way to reach a human in support.

product.title: Hi-Fi audio and fairer artist pay are the only reason niche services keep loyal users
product.plus: Tidal and Deezer hold on to audiophile subscribers through real lossless audio and more honest artist royalties. that is the sole reason users put up with the bugs.
product.minus: But the promised lossless quality sometimes silently degrades to lossy, and on some devices there is no output path to an external DAC.

product.title: Ads and paywalls on basic actions push listeners straight to a competitor
product.minus: Ads after every two songs. sometimes two or three back-to-back. plus paywalls on seeking, repeat, song selection, and lyrics. Listeners name exactly which competitor they are switching to.

product.title: Constant crashes and background battery drain
product.minus: The phone itself suggests putting the app into deep sleep because it keeps crashing in the background. It drains the battery, quits when you switch apps, and sometimes launches itself uninvited.

product.title: Paying for a subscription. but still getting ads
product.minus: The core grievance: the user paid, yet ads keep coming. often more than on free broadcast TV.

product.title: Paid once, then asked to pay again
product.minus: The subscription doesn't deliver what it promised: movies inside it require an extra rental fee, key content sits behind a higher tier, and "ad-free" turns out not to be fully ad-free.

product.title: Ads are louder than the show itself
product.minus: Ad volume is noticeably louder than the content. impossible to watch at night without keeping a hand on the volume control. A separate sensory irritant on top of the ads themselves.

product.title: Scrubbing backward triggers a whole new ad break
product.minus: Rewinding even ten seconds restarts a full ad block. Users become afraid to touch the timeline and get stuck in an ad loop.

product.title: Black (or green) screen. audio plays, picture gone
product.minus: A widespread Android defect: video drops to a black or green screen with only audio, fixed only by rebooting the phone. Often triggered by pausing or locking the screen.

product.title: App doesn't remember which episode you were on
product.minus: "Continue watching" resets: drops back to episode one of a finished season, to the final minutes of an episode, or to a different show entirely. Users have to find their place manually. and sit through extra ads.

product.title: Household checks kick out paying subscribers
product.minus: "One account, one household" enforcement hurts legitimate payers: kicked out while traveling, requiring confirmation from another device, forced to enter a code on every login.

product.title: Big match. servers go down
product.minus: The most painful live scenario: the service collapses during a major match (the World Cup). You paid for the event and couldn't watch it. Trust in paid live sports evaporates instantly.

product.title: Paid for sports, shown the crowd and the bench
product.minus: Even when the stream works, instead of the actual game users see fans, the dugout, or team buses. or commentary only in the wrong language. The broadcast rights exist. the product around them doesn't.

product.title: Paid for a dub that isn't in the player
product.minus: The content card promises a language track (Hindi, Tamil, English dub), the user subscribes. and that track is missing from the player. A direct bait-and-switch at the moment of purchase.

product.title: Canceling your subscription is nearly impossible
product.minus: The cancellation flow is a labyrinth: the button loops back, the link goes nowhere, "cancel" dumps you into the browse section. A dark pattern that turns leaving into a stressful ordeal.

product.title: Downloaded for offline. but won't open without internet
product.minus: Downloaded episodes are useless offline: the app won't launch on a plane or without a signal, and downloading requires keeping the app open. The main reason to download something is broken.

product.title: Good series get canceled. mid-watch
product.minus: Viewers invest weeks in a series that gets axed without a finale or pulled from the catalog mid-binge. It kills the urge to start any long show on the service.

product.title: An email address required for every profile. pure data harvesting
product.minus: Forcing an email onto every profile reads as data collection and resale. Users explicitly threaten to cancel over the invasive personal-data grab.

product.title: Player missing the basics: speed control, PiP, brightness
product.minus: Major services in 2026 lack what YouTube has had for years: playback speed, picture-in-picture, brightness and volume gestures, decent scrubbing. The player feels like a relic.

product.title: Every button needs to be pressed twice
product.minus: TV remote controls lag: pause, scrub, and episode selection only register on the second press after a delay. Users overshoot and land in the wrong place because of the lag.

product.title: Casting and cross-device sync keep breaking
product.minus: TV casting drops and restarts, the app doesn't sync with the browser, progress started on the phone doesn't carry over to the TV. The multi-screen scenario. the primary use case for streaming. is broken.

product.title: Can't remove anything from "Continue Watching"
product.minus: An accidental tap or trailer view permanently lodges something in the Continue Watching row with no way to remove it. The feed clogs up and stops reflecting what the viewer actually wants.

product.title: Free. but the ads make it unbearable
product.plus: Free access and a decent catalog are appreciated even in angry reviews. for many users it's a lifeline away from paid services.
product.minus: On free services there are so many ads that a 90-minute film stretches to three hours. ads play in HD while the film itself doesn't. many ads are for gambling or questionable content.

product.title: Forced AI in Private Conversations
product.minus: Messaging apps embedded ChatGPT and AI agents directly into the chat window. without consent and with a "disable" button that doesn't work. Users experience this as an intrusion into their private conversations and leave.

product.title: Device Lock Turns Your Account Into a Hostage
product.minus: Switch phones and lose everything. Migration requires the old, often dead device. number-based login gets quietly disabled in certain countries. years of messages, contacts, and purchased content vanish for good.

product.title: Bot Bans With No Explanation and No Human to Appeal To
product.minus: Accounts get auto-banned for "policy violations" with zero explanation. appeals are reviewed by the same bot. no human exists. yet actual spam and explicit channels sail through unmoderated.

product.title: Sign-Up and Login as an Obstacle Course
product.minus: New users can't even create an account: they need a friend's QR scan, must pay for an SMS code, face endless captchas, and hit "check your connection" errors. the app loses people on the very first screen.

product.title: Privacy as the Reason People Come. and the Reason They Leave
product.plus: End-to-end encryption and a non-commercial reputation are the only reasons people consciously switch apps and even donate money.

product.title: Feature Bloat Is Choking Simplicity
product.minus: Every update piles on feeds, wallets, stories, and ads. while the basic act of sending a message "barely works". People beg for a separate lightweight version of the app.

product.title: Scammers, Bots, and Predators With No Moderation
product.minus: Platforms are overrun with fraudsters, fake accounts, and predators. reports go nowhere. Safety. especially for children and vulnerable users. has become the biggest reputational hole.

product.title: Forced Redesigns and Mandatory Themes
product.minus: Updates forcibly change bubble colors and strip out beloved themes. with no way to revert. For users with light-sensitive eyes, this is physical discomfort, not just an aesthetic preference.

product.title: Memories and Archives Behind a Paywall
product.minus: Photos and history stored for free for years suddenly require a monthly subscription. Users feel ransomed for their own memories and bulk-export everything before deleting the app.

product.title: Messages Not Arriving. the Core Product Breaks
product.minus: The most basic function fails: notifications arrive tens of minutes late, messages sit unsent until the user manually opens the app. Any trust in the messenger collapses.

product.title: Ads Injected Into Personal Conversations
product.minus: Ads push into the message feed, pop up after calls, and redirect users to casinos and marketplaces. In Kik, they physically block the app until the phone is restarted.

product.title: One Account Per Device. a Nightmare for People With Multiple Lives
product.minus: Switching between personal and work profiles triggers "session expired", demands a second phone, and requires a separate number. The reality of two digital lives is completely ignored by the product.

product.title: Desktop and Multi-Device Experience Lags Far Behind Mobile
product.minus: There's no web version, or it barely functions. the linking QR code never loads. the desktop client wastes gigabytes of RAM. Cross-device is a weak spot even for privacy-first market leaders.

product.title: Network Effect Keeps People Trapped Even When They Hate the Product
product.minus: Users openly write that they stay only because "everyone else is there" or because they need to reach contacts in China or a specific country. This isn't loyalty. it's captivity, and it's an opening for migration.

product.title: Block Should Mean Block. the Failure to Protect Victims
product.minus: A blocked person still triggers notifications, copies your profile, and creates new accounts. For stalking and abuse victims, the "block" feature doesn't work. and the platform loses them entirely.

product.title: Mandatory Phone Numbers and Identity Checks Drive People Away
product.minus: Users are forced to hand over their number, passport, selfie, and full contact list just to have a simple chat. Growing age and ID verification requirements are pushing privacy-minded users to look for alternatives outside the US.

product.title: "Delivered". but your hands are empty
product.minus: The platform closes disputes based on a "delivered" courier status and refuses to refund money, even when the buyer proves the package never arrived.

product.title: They swap your cash refund for store credit
product.minus: Instead of returning money to your card, the platform automatically issues in-store credit that can't be spent all at once. you have to keep buying just to get your own money back.

product.title: What arrived isn't what was in the photo
product.minus: The item that shows up doesn't match the listing in material, color, or size. but the return window has either closed or proving the discrepancy is pointless.

product.title: Counterfeits and fakes, and the platform doesn't care
product.minus: Counterfeit goods are sold as genuine. even with unboxing video evidence the platform neither penalizes the seller nor issues a full refund.

product.title: The cart price is higher than the shelf price
product.minus: Add an item to your cart and the price silently multiplies. the promised checkout discount never materializes.

product.title: Free gifts that cost you money
product.minus: Slot-machine mechanics. "spin the wheel" and "pick 5 free gifts". pull you in, but at the finish line you're told to spend above a minimum or recruit friends, and the prize keeps moving.

product.title: Gamification gets in the way of just buying something
product.minus: Before you can search for anything, the app runs five minutes of spin wheels, pop-ups, and animations. some users report it literally makes them nauseous.

product.title: Forced AI search killed the results page
product.minus: Every query is routed through an AI assistant: it loads for minutes, returns four identical items instead of the full catalog, and there's no way to disable it.

product.title: Search and filters simply don't work
product.minus: Apply a filter to a search and the screen freezes on "searching" and never returns results. people miss auctions and give up and switch to the website.

product.title: Support is a bot that runs you in circles
product.minus: There's no reaching a real person: the AI chat replies with templates, closes tickets prematurely, and offers no path to escalate a real problem.

product.title: AI slop and dropshippers have crowded out real makers
product.minus: The handmade marketplace is flooded with AI-generated images and Temu resellers. there's no way to filter genuine creators from the slop, and stolen designs make it into curated picks.

product.title: Live streams have taken over the home screen
product.minus: Live sales and auto-playing videos are forced into the feed and search results with no way to opt out. the platform starts to look like a cheap carnival.

product.title: Fees and shipping eat all of a seller's earnings
product.minus: The marketplace takes 10% plus inflated shipping and pushes sellers to race to the bottom in price just to stay visible. so sellers move to platforms with no fees.

product.title: The platform automatically sides with the other party
product.minus: Disputes default against you: sellers see full refunds issued to buyers who already received the goods. buyers get denied even with clear proof of fraud.

product.title: Passport-and-selfie verification drives away long-time customers
product.minus: Sudden age verification requiring a photo ID and a selfie locks accounts of people with years of purchase history. even where the law doesn't require it.

product.title: Shipping costs only appear on the final screen
product.minus: An item is tagged "free shipping," but on the last step the price doubles because of logistics charges, and the only way to find out is to click a buried hyperlink.

product.title: Delivery brings the wrong item, a broken item, or half the order
product.minus: Couriers deliver the wrong product, someone else's order, or crushed packages. substitutions happen without notice, no delivery alerts. and you paid for both.

product.title: Unwanted subscriptions and unauthorized charges
product.minus: A saved card is used to silently enroll you in a paid subscription. you have to decline membership offers dozens of times per session.

product.title: Push notifications spam you like a clingy ex
product.minus: Dozens of pushes a day, animated banners in the notification shade, and emails about "gifts". turn them off in settings and an update quietly switches them back on.

product.title: Driver accepts the ride, then maneuvers the passenger into canceling first
product.minus: A driver accepts a ride, stalls for time, and forces the passenger to cancel. so the cancellation fee lands on the rider, not the driver

product.title: Pre-booking is really just a delayed search that falls apart
product.minus: A booking made days in advance assigns a driver, but 5 10 minutes before pickup the app starts searching from scratch. and finds nothing

product.title: The final fare is higher than the price shown at booking
product.minus: The amount charged doesn't match the estimate. a quiet upcharge called a "fare adjustment" appears with no explanation

product.title: No car shows up until you pay for "priority"
product.minus: Standard search spins forever, but the moment you pay for priority a driver appears instantly

product.title: Drivers demand cash on top of the in-app price
product.minus: A driver names a higher figure than shown in the app and insists on cash. or threatens to drop you off right there

product.title: When something goes wrong, there's only a looping bot
product.minus: At the worst possible moment, support is unreachable: an AI bot circles endlessly, replies are copy-pasted, human agents are nowhere to be found, and weeks pass in silence

product.title: Charged before the ride, no driver. refund never arrives
product.minus: Money is taken before the car shows up. when the driver never comes or the ride is canceled, the refund is held for weeks. or declared "processed" without ever arriving

product.title: Driver takes the long way around to run up the meter
product.minus: The driver deliberately goes the wrong way or takes a detour, blaming a broken GPS, and the fare doubles

product.title: Passenger safety is nobody's problem
product.minus: Reckless driving, aggression, being kicked out mid-trip. the platform disavows all responsibility and takes no action against the driver

product.title: inDrive drivers: "without us there's no app, and these rates are killing us"
product.minus: Drivers say passengers undercut fares below any reasonable floor, the commission is punishing, and rider no-shows go uncompensated

product.title: Tourist with a foreign number can't even sign up
product.minus: The app requires a local phone number and never delivers the code. the people who need a ride most are blocked at the front door

product.title: The stated pickup time is a systematic lie
product.minus: The app shows "2 minutes" before you book. after payment it jumps to 10 20 minutes, and the driver marked "3 minutes away" hasn't budged

product.title: No cars in rain or rush hour. exactly when you need one most
product.minus: At critical moments. downpour, early morning, a flight to catch. drivers are absent or ignoring requests, and the surge price spikes anyway

product.title: Same trip, same time: $9 today, $22 tomorrow, no explanation
product.minus: The identical route at the identical hour can cost two or three times as much from one day to the next, with no holiday, event, or traffic to justify it

product.title: Double-charged and the hold sits on the card for a week
product.minus: One ride triggers two charges or two holds, and the freeze takes 5 14 days to lift. riders need twice the fare in their account just in case

product.title: Ads and spam notifications take over the ride screen
product.minus: Full-screen banners cover the map and driver info during the trip. intrusive push notifications can't be turned off

product.title: Signed up for a subscription without consent, can't cancel
product.minus: Users are enrolled in paid subscriptions without asking. the cancel button is buried, and charges keep coming

product.title: Left something in the car. no way to reach the driver
product.minus: After a ride ends there's no channel to contact the driver, support goes silent, and lost items are never returned

product.title: Account closed for no reason. money frozen
product.minus: After years of use, the account is suddenly shut down with no reason given and no way to access your own money

product.title: Frozen funds = hunger, rent, stranded abroad
product.minus: When access to the account disappears, people are left with nothing for food, rent, or gas. sometimes stuck in a foreign country

product.title: In a crisis, you only get a bot
product.minus: When money is gone or the account is locked, there is no live person to reach: the bot loops, chat says "we'll get back to you" and never does

product.title: Money stolen. you lose the dispute
product.minus: Fraudulent charges are confirmed, but the dispute is rejected within days. the bank sides with the merchant or the thief and issues no refund

product.title: They won't let you open an account. but they kept your data
product.minus: Identity verification fails with a vague "legal reasons" rejection, video verification loops endlessly, and the submitted passport and selfie cannot be deleted

product.title: An app update locks you out of your money
